newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam sees rubber output jump over next decade.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam sees rubber output jump over next decade.

text.p: Vietnam's output of rubber is expected to rise by 50 percent over the next decade to 300,000 tonnes a year, with two-thirds of production being exported, the official Vietnam News Agency (VNA) said on Thursday.
The country now has some 250,000 hectares (617,750 acres) of rubber plantations with a total annual output of about 200,000 tonnes of dried latex.
VNA said the rubber-growing area would be expanded to 350,000 to 400,000 hectares (864,850 to 988,400 acres) over the next 10 years.

The Association of Natural Rubber Producing Countries (ANRPC) said on Tuesday that Vietnam had become its eighth member, joining India, Indonesia, Malaysia, Papua New Guinea, Singapore, Sri Lanka and Thailand.
ANRPC members now account for 85 percent of world output of natural rubber. Vietnam contributed close to two percent of world rubber production in 1995.
